Hi!

According to modern feminism, the phrase "can you make me a sandwich" is an insult that offends one to the very core (particularly if the asked is a woman and the person asking is a man). Now, ideas designed to cause conflicts wouldn't normally be a problem if everybody is in agreement that the idea is stupid, but this one has gotten some traction among some of the female youth. So here are my thoughts on why this is a silly mindset to have.

The phrase "can you make me a sandwich" has been misconstrued to be a form of oppression by the inner patriarchy of a man spilling out over the woman. I would argue that making a sandwich, or anything that is eaten, is not a form of oppression but a form of giving love via an action. For example, is giving someone a foot rub a form of oppression? Is fixing someone's computer a form of oppression? Heck, is hugging someone when they are sad a form of oppression? As you're probably realizing, asking your loved one to do something for you is not a form of oppression, regardless of which gender it is that is doing the asking.

I have some experience with the whole "making a sandwich" thing when I was in a relationship a while back. We used to occasionally make snacks for one another, and occasionally those snacks were sandwiches. So instead of preparing our own snacks, we prepared each other's. It is the strangest thing really, because even though the snacks we prepared were usually identical to when we did our own snacks, it felt and tasted a lot better when our loved one did it. It's almost as if she infused the snack with love, and indirectly fed me with her love (as corny as that sounds).

If you're in a relationship, you should try it. Heck, it doesn't even have to be a relationship, just with anyone you have mutual love with. Siblings, parents, significant other, etc. It's nice. Go and express your love.
My thoughts on the whole "make me a sandwich" thing

I think the use of the statement is often linked by the person saying it to be a sexist or belittling thing. The colloquial use of the term is what makes it a shitty one. But when used sincerely as you describe I think it actually is a good thing, as a matter of fact when I talk to people about sandwiches (since I love eating them) occasionally they'll mention that they would love to make me one. Because they also have interest in sandwiches, and sandwiches that are made for you are always really satisfying. And I realize that my phrasing here makes me sound like part of some weird sandwich cult.
